correctness.rationale: The strictly concave dual has unique constant optimum c=−ερ/(ε+2ρ) log(κ/n), with block derivatives DT_g=−τWᵀ and DT_f=−τW. The two-block F Jacobian on (f,g) is triangular with upper-left τ²WWᵀ and overwrites g; positive doubly stochastic W has simple constant singular value one and s<1 on 1⊥ by strict Jensen/Perron. Exact scalar translation maximizer δ=(ρ/2)log(mean e^(-f/ρ)/mean e^(-g/ρ)) gives Dδ=0.5(mean dg−mean df); after two raw updates the recovered constant-mode multiplier is −τ(1−τ)/2, while nonuniform eigenvalues remain τ²σ_j(W)². Thus q_G=max of this magnitude and τ²s², proving both thresholds and equality. Independently built nonlinear finite-difference Jacobians for n=2,3,5 and five ε/ρ ratios (15 parameter cases × F/G), including nonsymmetric W, agree; finite differences are corroboration, not all-n proof.
